name: Jack Newton
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Clio (legal practice management / legal AI software, Vancouver)
profile: Canadian software entrepreneur who co-founded Clio in 2008 with Rian Gauvreau, pioneering cloud-based practice management for lawyers. In Nov 2025 Clio closed the US$1B acquisition of vLex (largest legal-tech M&A ever) alongside a US$500M Series G at a US$5B valuation; Newton is pushing Clio into AI-powered legal research and workflows.
interesting_fact: The vLex deal was described as the largest M&A transaction ever in legal technology, and was announced together with a US$500M Series G at a US$5B valuation.
deep_cut_fact: Before Clio, he was the first software developer at Chenomx, a University of Alberta spinoff building an NMR-based medical diagnostic tool, and took a sabbatical from it to do an MSc in machine learning under Russ Greiner; he started programming around age eight on an IBM 8086.
notes: Very public CEO; author of 'The Client-Centered Law Firm'; frequent conference keynoter (ClioCon). Press route via Clio media team.

profile: Could not verify any link between a Jay Scannell and MOLOCO. Moloco's published co-founders are Ikkjin Ahn (CEO), David Sehyuk Park and Donghwan Jeon (founded 2013). The only public Jay Scannell found is an exec at Prototype Productions (ex-SkyMall, GiftCards.com), unrelated to Moloco.

name: Kanav Hasija
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Customer Officer (previously Chief Product Officer), Innovaccer (San Francisco)
profile: IIT Kharagpur graduate who co-founded healthcare data/AI company Innovaccer with Abhinav Shashank and Sandeep Gupta. He built the company's Data Activation Platform underlying its Health Cloud. Innovaccer raised a US$275M Series F in Jan 2025 (backers incl. B Capital, Kaiser Permanente, M12), with press estimates above US$3B valuation.
interesting_fact: Innovaccer's Series F in January 2025 drew strategic health-system investors such as Kaiser Permanente and Banner Health alongside Microsoft's M12 and Danaher Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he went to the US after IIT Kharagpur to earn a master's in patent law at the University of New Hampshire; as an undergrad he interned at General Electric and was a principal consultant at the student-run Kharagpur Consulting Group.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Abhinav Shashank. Press email is the named press contact on Innovaccer's Jan 2025 release; may change.

name: Jannick Malling
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, Public (Public.com investing platform, New York)
profile: Danish fintech entrepreneur who co-founded the multi-asset investing platform Public with Leif Abraham and runs it as co-CEO. Earlier he worked at Saxo Bank, was Head of Product at CFH Group and co-founded trading-API startup Tradable. Public has recently pushed into direct indexing, bonds and AI-driven 'agentic brokerage' features.
interesting_fact: Public's userbase roughly doubled within days during the January 2021 GameStop frenzy, after having grown 13x the year before, per Malling.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Copenhagen he built websites to organise video-game meetups, and he joined Saxo Bank at 17; he credits that early stint with teaching him speed and user-centric design, and later collaborated with ex-Saxo colleagues on new ventures.
notes: Shares CEO role with Leif Abraham; has spoken publicly (Stanford eCorner) about the co-CEO model. Frequent podcast guest on fintech topics.

name: Anderson Sumarli
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Ajaib Group (Indonesian investment app; also President Commissioner of Ajaib Sekuritas)
profile: Indonesian fintech founder who started Ajaib with Stanford GSB classmate Yada Piyajomkwan; it went through Y Combinator (S18) and became Southeast Asia's first investment-fintech unicorn, offering stocks, mutual funds and crypto. Ajaib also controls Bank Bumi Artha (BNBA). In Aug 2026 it raised a US$270M Series C led by SBI Group at a valuation above its prior ~US$1B mark.
interesting_fact: Ajaib's US$270M Series C (Aug 2026), led by Japan's SBI Group, was reported as Indonesia's biggest tech funding round since 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Ajaib he studied Applied Economics & Management at Cornell (summa cum laude), worked in IBM's Chief Analytics Office (2014-16) and was a BCG consultant (2016-18), then did his MBA at Stanford GSB.
notes: No published press email found on Ajaib's site. Stanford GSB has a case study on Ajaib (useful conversation hook). EY Indonesia 2022 Young Entrepreneur Award; Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2020.

name: Henrik Müller-Hansen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Gelato (on-demand print/production software, Oslo/Fornebu); board member, Patricia Industries (since Jan 2025)
profile: Norwegian-based entrepreneur, former CEO of Tele2 Norway, who launched Optimalprint around 2007 and then Gelato in 2012. Gelato's software and network route print-on-demand orders to local production hubs in 30+ countries, cutting transport distance and waste; it also sells GelatoConnect, a production OS for print factories. Gelato reached a US$1B+ valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Gelato's model is a 'local on-demand production' network: orders are produced in partner factories near the end customer across 30+ countries rather than shipped from a central plant.
deep_cut_fact: Before studying at the Stockholm School of Economics he served as a team leader in a military Underwater Demolition Team; as CEO of Tele2 Norway (2003-06) he roughly doubled revenue from NOK 1.5bn to 3.2bn.
notes: Gelato press releases name a VP PR & Communications (Julie Ryland, 2025) but email addresses are obfuscated on the pages; route via gelato.com news/press section. Tele2 revenue figure is from Gelato's leadership page (https://www.gelato.com/leadership).

name: Artavazd Mehrabyan
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Picsart (creative/AI photo-video editing platform, Armenia/US)
profile: Armenian software engineer who co-founded Picsart with Hovhannes Avoyan and Mikayel Vardanyan (c.2011), serving first as COO and later as CTO. Picsart grew to ~150M monthly active users and 1B+ downloads and became Armenia's first unicorn (2021). He now leads Picsart's push into generative AI, including a commercially safe image model built with Getty Images.
interesting_fact: Picsart reached about 150 million monthly active users and over one billion downloads, and partnered with Getty Images in 2024 on a commercially safe text-to-image model.
deep_cut_fact: Before Picsart he was a chief software architect (incl. at Lycos Europe, Sourcio and Virtual Solutions); he holds two master's degrees: Industrial Engineering from the Armenian National Agrarian University and Computer Science from the American University of Armenia.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Hovhannes Avoyan is the public face. Good angle: Picsart's AI/GPU infrastructure and Armenia's tech ecosystem. Prior-employer list from a job-board company profile; degrees from conference speaker bio.

name: Moses Lo
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Xendit Group (Southeast Asian payments infrastructure, Jakarta)
profile: Australian-born founder (UNSW, UC Berkeley MBA; ex-BCG and Amazon) who co-founded Xendit in 2015; it went through Y Combinator S15 and became the first YC unicorn from Indonesia. Xendit provides payment APIs across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, and in Nov 2025 launched a Global Account product at the Singapore FinTech Festival.
interesting_fact: Xendit was among the first five Southeast Asian companies accepted into Y Combinator, and became Indonesia's first YC unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: At Radford College in Canberra (Class of 2005) he won debating tournaments and represented Australia at Model United Nations; his advice to students is that 'marks are less important than soft skills.'
notes: Accessible, frequent podcast/conference speaker (Money20/20 Asia). Press email is the named PR & Communications contact on Xendit's Nov 2025 release; based in Jakarta.
